b: In modern time, bedtime routines are very common for both children and adults. You might put on pajamas, brush your teeth, turn down the lights and read, or crack open a beer and turn the TV on until you fall asleep in an easy chair (not recommended, but you do you). Children can have even more structured routines that start to resemble Imperial Chinese court functions in their number of steps and elaborate choreography (and the penalties paid for violating the established order). Do we have any record of ancient Roman bedtime habits? What people wore, how they got ready for bed, what they slept on, etc? I would welcome answers for any age, gender, or social status.
